ios.desc:
Foxi isn’t just another spending tracker. It’s a budgeting app designed to help you stay on track — whether you spend on debit or credit cards.

By comparing your predicted balance with your actual balance, Foxi shows whether you're ahead, behind, or right where you should be. That clarity makes it easier to plan, adjust, and stay in control of your money day by day.

Spreadsheets give you power but are clunky on a phone. Other budgeting apps can feel overwhelming or too basic. Foxi brings the best of both worlds: simple, powerful budgeting that’s built for mobile.

Key features:
• Balance comparison — see if you’re ahead, behind, or on track
• Daily outlook — predicted bills, subscriptions, and annual costs
• Smarter expenses — mandatory, discretionary, and annual, adjusted for your pay cycle
• Income view — add net and gross pay, with deductions
• Subscriptions view — track recurring costs in one place
• Funds & pots — manage flexible spending or save toward goals
• Data backup — simple copy & paste code
• No accounts or sign-ups — your data stays with you
• Clean, fast, and built to be stress-free

Foxi makes balancing your budget simple, realistic, and convenient — on your phone, with or without credit cards.

Download Foxi today and take control of your finances.

show_hn.title: Show HN: I made a budgeting app to budget properly

quotes.text:
Hi everyone,

I’ve been working on a little side project and would love some feedback. It’s a budgeting app I made called Foxi: Budget Planner Tracker (on iOS).

The reason I built it is honestly because I didn't find that the other apps worked for me — I’ve always struggled with budgeting apps. Most feel like spending trackers, or they’re so complicated that I end up giving up. Spreadsheets are the only thing that’s ever really worked for me, but they get messy fast and aren’t fun to manage on a phone.

So I tried to make something I’d actually want to use:

- A real budget, with the flexibility of sheets but without the overhead
- Clean and simple UI
- Balance comparison (important one for me)
- No accounts or sign-ups (I hate when apps force that on you)
- A way to back up your budget easily if you ever need to move it

I’d really appreciate any thoughts — whether that’s features you’d want, things that feel missing, or just general feedback.

Thanks a lot!
